claim: Rfng is significantly upregulated in Paneth cells compared to Lgr5+ CBCs based on microarray data.
source: We analysed previously published microarray data on Lgr5+ CBCs and Paneth cells (Sato et al., 2011) and found that Rfng is significantly upregulated in Paneth cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of published microarray data cited from Sato et al., 2011, and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Paneth cells are enriched for Rfng as measured by RT-qPCR.
source: We isolated CBCs and Paneth cells (CD24high/SSChigh) from Lgr5-GFP mice by FACS using an established protocol (Sato et al., 2011; Sato et al., 2009) and found that the Paneth cells are enriched for Rfng (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1A, using cells isolated by FACS following established protocols cited from Sato et al., 2011 and 2009.

claim: Rfng is enriched in Paneth cells as confirmed by RNA in situ hybridisation.
source: We also confirmed that Rfng is enriched in the Paneth cells by RNA in situ hybridisation (ISH) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA ISH data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The colony forming efficiency of Rfng KD CBCs was reduced compared to the control.
source: The colony formation efficiency of the Rfng KD CBCs was reduced compared to the control (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The number of Lgr5+ CBCs decreased after Rfng loss in organoids, whereas the number of Paneth cells remained relatively unchanged.
source: Flow cytometric analysis showed that the number of Lgr5+ CBCs decreased after Rfng loss, whereas the number of Paneth cells remained relatively unchanged (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Rfng−/− mice had almost a two-fold depletion in CBCs.
source: Analysis revealed that the Rfng−/− mice had almost a two-fold depletion in CBCs (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of Rfng−/− mice shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A reduction of CBC marker Lgr5 transcripts in the crypts harvested from Rfng−/− mouse intestines was observed by RT-qPCR measurement when compared to the control.
source: A reduction of CBC marker Lgr5 transcripts in the crypts harvested from Rfng−/− mouse intestines was observed by RT-qPCR measurement when compared to the control (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1F comparing Rfng−/− and control mice.

claim: The number of Paneth and goblet cells remain largely unchanged after loss of Rfng in vivo.
source: The number of Paneth and goblet cells remain largely unchanged and no other significant phenotype was detected in the epithelium (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F.

claim: The colony formation ability of CBCs incubated with Paneth cells lacking Rfng was significantly lower than the control in the Organoid Reconstitution Assay.
source: We find that the colony formation ability of CBCs incubated with Paneth cells lacking Rfng was significantly lower than the control (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by Organoid Reconstitution Assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Notch target genes Hes1 and Hey1 have reduced expression in the CBCs upon loss of Rfng.
source: Western blotting shows that Notch target genes Hes1 and Hey1 have reduced expression in the CBCs upon loss of Rfng.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data described in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The levels of ligands DLL1, four and JAG1 on Paneth cells were not significantly altered after Rfng loss, consistent with the post-translational modifying role of Fringe.
source: However, the levels of ligands DLL1, four and JAG1 on Paneth cells were not significantly altered, consistent with the post-translational modifying role of Fringe (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 2A and is consistent with established knowledge about Fringe function.

claim: Rfng shRNA decreased the mean RBPJκ-dsRed fluorescent intensity, indicating reduced overall Notch signalling in CBCs.
source: Rfng shRNA decreased the mean RBPJκ-dsRed fluorescent intensity, indicating reduced overall Notch signalling in CBCs.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of RBPJκ-dsRed reporter activity described in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Paneth cells express the ligand Dll1.
source: We confirmed that the Paneth cells express the ligand Dll1 by RNA-ISH (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-ISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mean fluorescent intensity of NOTCH1 binding to Paneth cells with Rfng knockdown was reduced compared to the scrambled control.
source: Mean fluorescent intensity (MFI) of NOTCH1 binding to Paneth cells with Rfng knockdown was reduced compared to the scrambled control.
evidence: The claim is supported by ligand availability assay data using flow cytometry described in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: DLL1 and DLL4 levels on the Paneth cell surface reduced after the loss of Rfng.
source: Flow cytometry showed that DLL1 and DLL4 levels on the Paneth cell surface reduced after the loss of Rfng (Figure 2D), although the total expression level of DLL1 and DLL4 within Paneth cells is not changed by Rfng knockdown after the cells were permeabilised (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data on unpermeabilised cells shown in Figure 2D, with comparison to permeabilised cells in Figure 2E.

claim: The total expression level of DLL1 and DLL4 within Paneth cells is not changed by Rfng knockdown after the cells were permeabilised.
source: Flow cytometry showed that DLL1 and DLL4 levels on the Paneth cell surface reduced after the loss of Rfng (Figure 2D), although the total expression level of DLL1 and DLL4 within Paneth cells is not changed by Rfng knockdown after the cells were permeabilised (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data on permeabilised cells shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Western blotting confirmed that the total DLL1 and DLL4 expression in Paneth cells does not change significantly after the loss of Rfng.
source: Western blotting also confirmed that the total DLL1 and DLL4 expression in Paneth cells does not change significantly after the loss of Rfng (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Gene expression levels of Lgr5 and Notch components were comparable between Sc. Control and Mfng KD organoids.
source: Gene expression levels of Lgr5 and Notch components were comparable between Sc. Control and Mfng KD organoids (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The colony forming efficiency of Mfng shRNA-expressing CBCs was similar to the scrambled control.
source: Additionally, the colony forming efficiency (Figure 3C) and the expression pattern of Lgr5-GFP (CBC) and MUC2 (goblet cells) (Figure 3D) of Mfng shRNA-expressing CBCs were similar to the scrambled control.
evidence: The claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The expression pattern of Lgr5-GFP (CBC) and MUC2 (goblet cells) of Mfng shRNA-expressing CBCs was similar to the scrambled control.
source: Additionally, the colony forming efficiency (Figure 3C) and the expression pattern of Lgr5-GFP (CBC) and MUC2 (goblet cells) (Figure 3D) of Mfng shRNA-expressing CBCs were similar to the scrambled control.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Flow cytometry confirmed no significant change in the number of Lgr5-GFP+ CBCs and goblet cells after Mfng knockdown.
source: We quantified this observation using flow cytometry, which confirmed no significant change in the number of Lgr5-GFP+ CBCs and goblet cells (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: The percentage of differentiated cells, identified by CK20 expression, was not significantly altered between Sc. control and Mfng KD organoids.
source: Finally, the percentage of differentiated cells, identified by CK20 expression, was not significantly altered between Sc. control and Mfng KD organoids (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The number of goblet cells was not significantly altered in Mfng+/+ mice compared to Mfng−/− mice based on immunofluorescence.
source: Quantification in intestinal tissues based on IF expression indicated that the number of goblet cells was not significantly altered in Mfng+/+ mice compared to Mfng−/− mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data described in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The total number of CK20+ cells in intestines was similar in wild-type and Mfng null mice.
source: Finally, we examined the total number of CK20+ cells in intestines, which was similar in wild-type and Mfng null mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Goblet cells were slightly enriched in Mfng when compared to the CBCs.
source: We observed that goblet cells were slightly enriched in Mfng when compared to the CBCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: No significant change in the cell surface expression of DLLs on goblet cells was found after the loss of Mfng.
source: We found no significant change in the cell surface expression of DLLs on goblet cells after the loss of Mfng (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F.

claim: Mfng plays an insignificant role in intestinal tissues.
source: Overall, these data suggest Mfng plays an insignificant role in intestinal tissues.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective data showing no significant phenotypic changes after Mfng loss.

claim: Lfng is expressed by a subset of cells in the upper crypt (transient-amplifying cell region) and villus.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis of intestines from Lfng-GFP reporter mice confirmed that Lfng is expressed by a subset of cells in the upper crypt (transient-amplifying cell region) and villus (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from Lfng-GFP reporter mice shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Lfng-GFP+ cells are post-mitotic in the upper-crypt.
source: We observe that Lfng-GFP+ cells are post-mitotic in the upper-crypt. (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Lfng-GFP+ cells express ChgA, Dclk1 or Muc2 which are markers for enteroendocrine, Tuft or goblet cells respectively.
source: Further analysis showed that these Lfng-GFP+ cells express ChgA, Dclk1 or Muc2 which are markers for enteroendocrine, Tuft or goblet cells respectively (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence co-staining data shown in Figure 4B–D.

claim: In the upper crypt, immunofluorescence analysis showed Notch1 activity in the cells adjacent to Lfng-GFP+ cells but not in themselves.
source: In the upper crypt, immunofluorescence analysis showed Notch1 activity in the cells adjacent to Lfng-GFP+ cells but not in themselves (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing NICD expression shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Lfng is in goblet cells and not CBCs as confirmed by RT-qPCR.
source: We performed RT-qPCR measurement of Lfng using goblet cells and CBCs isolated from Lgr5-GFP mice and confirmed that Lfng is in goblet cells and not CBCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The number of goblet cells (MUC2+) increased after the loss of Lfng in organoids.
source: However, we find that the number of goblet cells (MUC2+) increased after the loss of Lfng (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The number of goblet cells (UEA-1+/CD24-) was increased significantly in Lfng KD organoids (5.5% of the total population) when compared to the scrambled control (1.9%).
source: Quantification by flow cytometry showed that number of goblet cells (UEA-1+/CD24-) (Wong et al., 2012) was increased significantly in Lfng KD organoids (5.5% of the total population) when compared to the scrambled control (1.9%) (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4G, with citation to Wong et al., 2012 for the goblet cell markers.

claim: The ratio of the number of goblet cells to Lgr5+ CBCs increased approximately three times in Lfng shRNA-expressing organoids.
source: Accordingly, the ratio of the number of goblet cells to Lgr5+ CBCs increased approximately three times in Lfng shRNA-expressing organoids (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: An increase in the number of goblet cells was observed in the Lfng null mice.
source: We observed an increase in the number of goblet cells in the Lfng null mice as expected (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Immunofluorescence analysis based on MUC2 expression in small intestinal tissues from Lfng−/− mice showed an increase in the number of goblet cells when compared to the control (Lfng+/+) mice.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis based on MUC2 expression in small intestinal tissues from Lfng−/− mice showed an increase in the number of goblet cells when compared to the control (Lfng+/+) mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Using flow cytometry, 14.1% of small intestinal cells in Lfng−/− mice are goblet cells, which is significantly higher than the 7.9% goblet cells in the small intestine of wild-type litter-mate control mice.
source: Finally, using flow cytometry we quantified goblet cell numbers in Lfng−/− mice: 14.1% of small intestinal cells, which is significantly higher than the 7.9% goblet cells in the small intestine of wild-type litter-mate control mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: No change in the Paneth cell numbers was observed after loss of Lfng.
source: We observed no change in the Paneth cell numbers after loss of Lfng (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: RT-qPCR measurements indicated decreased Hes1 and increased Atoh1 expression in Lfng−/− progenitors compared to the control.
source: RT-qPCR measurements indicated decreased Hes1 and increased Atoh1 (transcriptional factor essential for generating secretory lineage (Shroyer et al., 2007)) expression in Lfng−/− progenitors compared to the control.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data described in the text and shown in Figure 5D, with citation to Shroyer et al., 2007 for Atoh1 function.

claim: Reduced activated Notch1 (NICD) was confirmed in the upper crypts of Lfng null mice intestines.
source: We also confirmed reduced activated Notch1 (NICD) in the upper crypts of Lfng null mice intestines (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Secreted Lfng was detected at a concentration of approximately 315–325 ng/mL in organoid culture medium using two independent LFNG primary antibodies.
source: Secreted Lfng was detected at a concentration of approximately 315–325 ng/mL using two independent LFNG primary antibodies (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RFNG and MFNG were not detected in the organoid culture medium.
source: The other Fringes, RFNG and MFNG, were not detected in the culture medium (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The percentage of goblet cells remained similar to the Lfng knockdown (shRNA) condition and significantly higher than scrambled shRNA-expressing organoids after incubation with soluble LFNG.
source: After 24 hr, organoid cultures were analysed using flow cytometry, which showed that the percentage of goblet cells remained similar to the Lfng knockdown (shRNA) condition and significantly higher than scrambled shRNA-expressing organoids which express endogenous LFNG (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The expression levels of Notch ligands DLL1 and DLL4 were similar between Lfng knockdown with and without soluble LFNG.
source: RT-qPCR revealed that the expression levels of Notch ligands DLL1 and DLL4 were similar between Lfng knockdown with and without soluble LFNG (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: IF analysis based on MUC2 expression in small intestinal tissues from RLfng mice showed similar goblet cell numbers in villus crypt units compared to wild-type (Lfng+/+) mice.
source: IF analysis based on MUC2 expression in small intestinal tissues from RLfng mice showed similar goblet cell numbers in villus crypt units compared to wild-type (Lfng+/+) mice (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The effect of LFNG on goblet cell numbers and intestinal homeostasis is not dependent on its secreted form.
source: Taken together, our in vitro and in vivo findings suggest that the effect of LFNG on goblet cell numbers and intestinal homeostasis is not dependent on its secreted form.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined in vitro and in vivo experimental results showing no functional role for secreted LFNG.

claim: Mean fluorescent intensity of NOTCH1 binding to goblet cells with Lfng knockdown was reduced compared to the control.
source: Mean fluorescent intensity of NOTCH1 binding to goblet cells with Lfng knockdown was reduced compared to the control, suggesting that the ligands available on the goblet cell surface for NOTCH1 to bind to were reduced after the loss of Lfng.
evidence: The claim is supported by ligand availability assay data using flow cytometry described in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: DLL1 and DLL4 levels on the goblet cell surface reduced after the loss of Lfng.
source: Flow cytometry shows that DLL1 and DLL4 levels, detected using specific antibodies, on the goblet cell surface reduced after the loss of Lfng (Figure 7B), although the total expression of DLL1 and DLL4 by the goblet cells measured after the permeabilising the cells remained almost the same (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data on unpermeabilised cells shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The total expression of DLL1 and DLL4 by the goblet cells measured after permeabilising the cells remained almost the same after Lfng loss.
source: Flow cytometry shows that DLL1 and DLL4 levels, detected using specific antibodies, on the goblet cell surface reduced after the loss of Lfng (Figure 7B), although the total expression of DLL1 and DLL4 by the goblet cells measured after the permeabilising the cells remained almost the same (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data on permeabilised cells shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Western blotting confirmed that the total DLL1 and DLL4 expression in goblet cells does not change significantly after the loss of Lfng.
source: Western blotting also confirmed that the total DLL1 and DLL4 expression in goblet cells does not change significantly after the loss of Lfng (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Rfng is enriched in the Paneth cells and promotes cell surface expression of DLL1 and DLL4.
source: We report that Rfng is enriched in the Paneth cells and promotes cell surface expression of DLL1 and DLL4.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data including RT-qPCR, ISH, and flow cytometry showing Rfng expression in Paneth cells and its effect on DLL surface expression.

claim: RFNG promotes Notch activity in the neighbouring Lgr5+ CBCs assisting their self-renewal.
source: This promotes Notch activity in the neighbouring Lgr5+ CBCs assisting their self-renewal.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing reduced Notch activity and CBC numbers after Rfng loss.

claim: Mfng does not appear to contribute significantly in maintaining the epithelium.
source: Mfng does not appear to contribute significantly in maintaining the epithelium.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing no significant phenotypic changes after Mfng loss in vitro and in vivo.

claim: Lfng is expressed by enteroendocrine, Tuft and goblet cells and suppresses the secretory lineage.
source: Lfng on the other hand is expressed by enteroendocrine, Tuft and goblet cells and suppresses the secretory lineage (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing Lfng expression in these cell types and functional data showing increased goblet cells after Lfng loss.

claim: Fringe proteins are present in the ligand-presenting 'sender' secretory cells and promote Notch activity in the neighbouring 'receiver' cells in the intestinal epithelium.
source: Hence, in the intestinal epithelium, Fringes are present in the ligand-presenting 'sender' secretory cells and promote Notch activity in the neighbouring 'receiver' cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective data showing Fringe expression in ligand-expressing cells and their effects on Notch activity in adjacent cells.

claim: Fringes provide for targeted modulation of Notch activity and thus the cell fate in the stem cell zone, or the upper crypt and villus.
source: Fringes thereby provide for targeted modulation of Notch activity and thus the cell fate in the stem cell zone, or the upper crypt and villus.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the spatial expression patterns of Fringes and their effects on Notch signaling in different intestinal compartments.

claim: Lgr5+ Crypt Base Columnar cells (CBCs) located at the bottom of the crypts constantly self-renew to maintain the small intestinal epithelium.
source: Lgr5+ Crypt Base Columnar cells (CBCs) located at the bottom of the crypts constantly self-renew to maintain the small intestinal epithelium, which is one of the fastest regenerative tissues in the body (Barker et al., 2007; van der Flier et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Barker et al., 2007 and van der Flier et al., 2009, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: CBCs divide and move up the crypt into the progenitor or transit-amplifying zone where the cells rapidly proliferate and terminally differentiate into two major types: absorptive (enterocytes) and secretory (mainly Paneth and goblet cells).
source: CBCs divide and move up the crypt into the progenitor or transit-amplifying zone where the cells rapidly proliferate and terminally differentiate into two major types: absorptive (enterocytes) and secretory (mainly Paneth and goblet cells).
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about intestinal epithelial cell differentiation.

claim: Enterocytes and goblet cells populate the villi while the Paneth cells move to the bottom of the crypt and provide a niche for the CBCs.
source: Enterocytes and goblet cells populate the villi while the Paneth cells move to the bottom of the crypt and provide a niche for the CBCs (van der Flier et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to van der Flier et al., 2009, representing established knowledge.

claim: Upon activation of a Notch receptor by a ligand, it undergoes successive cleavages by ADAM/TACE and γ-secretase.
source: Upon activation of a Notch receptor by a ligand, it undergoes successive cleavages by ADAM/TACE and γ-secretase (Bray, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Bray, 2006, representing established knowledge about Notch signaling.

claim: The cleaved intracellular domain (NICD) translocates to the nucleus leading to the transcription of multiple genes such as Hes and Hey families.
source: The cleaved intracellular domain (NICD) translocates to the nucleus leading to the transcription of multiple genes such as Hes and Hey families (Kopan, 2002; Iso et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kopan, 2002 and Iso et al., 2003, representing established knowledge about Notch signaling.

claim: The extracellular domain of the Notch receptor and ligands contain EGF-like repeats, some of which serve as substrates for O-fucosylation by POFUT1.
source: The extracellular domain of the Notch receptor and ligands contain EGF-like repeats, some of which serve as substrates for O-fucosylation by POFUT1 (Rampal et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rampal et al., 2007 and Wang et al., 2001, representing established knowledge.

claim: The fucosylated product may be further modified within the Golgi network by Fringe proteins: Lunatic (LFNG), Manic (MFNG) and Radical Fringe (RFNG).
source: The fucosylated product may be further modified within the Golgi network by Fringe proteins: Lunatic (LFNG), Manic (MFNG) and Radical Fringe (RFNG) (Moloney et al., 2000; Haines and Irvine, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Moloney et al., 2000 and Haines and Irvine, 2003, representing established knowledge.

claim: Fringe proteins are typically expressed in receptor-expressing 'receiver' cells.
source: Fringe proteins are typically expressed in receptor-expressing 'receiver' cells (Haines and Irvine, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Haines and Irvine, 2003, representing established knowledge.

claim: Glycosylation of NOTCH1 by LFNG and MFNG increases its activation by DLL1 but decreases its activation by JAG1.
source: Glycosylation of NOTCH1 by LFNG and MFNG increases its activation by DLL1 but decreases its activation by JAG1 (Haines and Irvine, 2003; Hicks et al., 2000; Panin et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Haines and Irvine, 2003; Hicks et al., 2000; and Panin et al., 1997, representing established knowledge.

claim: Glycosylation by RFNG increases the activation of NOTCH1 by both DLL1 and JAG1.
source: In contrast, glycosylation by RFNG increases the activation of NOTCH1 by both DLL1 and JAG1 (LeBon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to LeBon et al., 2014, representing established knowledge.

claim: At the bottom of the crypt, Notch signalling is important for the maintenance of CBCs.
source: At the bottom of the crypt, Notch signalling is important for the maintenance of CBCs (Pellegrinet et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Pellegrinet et al., 2011, representing established knowledge.

claim: In the upper crypt, Notch activity, mainly through Hes1, is essential for the enterocyte differentiation.
source: In the upper crypt however, Notch activity, mainly through Hes1, is essential for the enterocyte differentiation (van der Flier et al., 2009; Fre et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to van der Flier et al., 2009 and Fre et al., 2005, representing established knowledge.

claim: Inhibition of Notch signalling results in the loss of proliferative CBCs and progenitor cells and leads to their differentiation into goblet cells in the upper crypt and villus.
source: Inhibition of Notch signalling results in the loss of proliferative CBCs and progenitor cells and leads to their differentiation into goblet cells in the upper crypt and villus, indicating the importance of the pathway in maintaining the tissue (Pellegrinet et al., 2011; VanDussen et al., 2012; Riccio et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pellegrinet et al., 2011; VanDussen et al., 2012; Riccio et al., 2008; and Wu et al., 2010, representing established knowledge.

claim: Notch1, 2 and Dll1, 4 are known to be the necessary receptors and ligands in the intestine.
source: Notch1, 2 and Dll1, 4 are known to be the necessary receptors and ligands in the intestine (Pellegrinet et al., 2011; Riccio et al., 2008; Schröder and Gossler, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pellegrinet et al., 2011; Riccio et al., 2008; and Schröder and Gossler, 2002, representing established knowledge.

claim: The fringe proteins are known to be expressed in the intestine.
source: Although, the fringe proteins are known to be expressed in the intestine, their function has not been studied (Schröder and Gossler, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schröder and Gossler, 2002.

claim: The function of fringe proteins in the intestine has not been studied prior to this work.
source: Although, the fringe proteins are known to be expressed in the intestine, their function has not been studied (Schröder and Gossler, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schröder and Gossler, 2002 and represents a knowledge gap.

claim: Both RFNG and LFNG can increase the presence of DLL1 and DLL4 on the plasma membrane.
source: We have observed that both RFNG and LFNG can increase the presence of DLL1 and DLL4 on the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is supported by ligand availability assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Increased DLL presence on the plasma membrane can potentially contribute to the increase in cis-inhibition of NOTCH1 by DLL1 in the presence of fringe.
source: This can potentially contribute to the increase in cis-inhibition of NOTCH1 by DLL1 in the presence of fringe (LeBon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the data and citation to LeBon et al., 2014.

claim: Fringe modulation of ligands will be of significance in understanding Notch activity in cancer stem cell asymmetric division where LFNG, DLL1 and NOTCH1 are present in the same cell.
source: Fringe modulation of ligands will be of significance in understanding Notch activity in cancer stem cell asymmetric division where LFNG, DLL1 and NOTCH1 are present in the same cell (Bu et al., 2013; Bu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is speculative about future significance, supported by citations to Bu et al., 2013 and Bu et al., 2016.

claim: The mechanism behind the increase in cell-surface expression of the ligands still needs to be understood.
source: However, the mechanism behind the increase in cell-surface expression of the ligands still needs to be understood.
evidence: The claim acknowledges a knowledge gap based on the current findings.

claim: The glycosylation state of proteins has been known to affect their intracellular trafficking.
source: The glycosylation state of proteins has been known to affect their intracellular trafficking (Huet et al., 2003; Ohtsubo and Marth, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Huet et al., 2003 and Ohtsubo and Marth, 2006, representing established knowledge.

claim: Fringe mediated glycosylation or the addition of Galactose and Sialic acid post fringe activity might affect the trafficking of DLLs to the cell surface.
source: It raises the possibility that fringe mediated glycosylation or the addition of Galactose and Sialic acid post fringe activity might affect the trafficking of DLLs to the cell surface.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible mechanism based on inference.

claim: Lfng in the Dll1 expressing cell, in the presence of Dll3, is known to reduce Notch activity in the neighbouring cell.
source: Lfng in the Dll1 expressing cell, in the presence of Dll3, is known to reduce Notch activity in the neighbouring cell (Okubo et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Okubo et al., 2012, representing established knowledge.

claim: Ligands might interact with each other in the presence of Lfng which might explain the observed increase in DLL surface expression.
source: This raises the possibility that ligands interact with each other in the presence of Lfng which might explain our observation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible mechanism based on inference from cited work.

claim: The experiments cannot completely rule out the possibility that low levels of Rfng expression in CBCs can also contribute to the phenotype by directly modulating Notch receptors.
source: Also, our experiments cannot completely rule out the possibility that low levels of Rfng expression in CBCs (in comparison to Paneth cells) can also contribute to the phenotype by directly modulating Notch receptors.
evidence: The claim acknowledges a limitation of the experimental approach based on inference.

claim: Some mesenchymal cells express Rfng detectable by RNA ISH.
source: We have observed some mesenchymal cells also express Rfng detectable by RNA ISH.
evidence: The claim is based on observation from RNA ISH experiments.

claim: Some of the mesenchymal cells also express Dll1.
source: We also observe that some of the mesenchymal cells also express Dll1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on observation from RNA ISH shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mesenchyme can provide Notch ligands to the Lgr5+ CBCs in vivo.
source: This raises the possibility that the mesenchyme can also provide Notch ligands to the Lgr5 + CBCs in vivo.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the observation of ligand expression in mesenchymal cells.

claim: Rfng promotes cell surface expression of Dll1 in mesenchymal cells.
source: This raises the possibility that the mesenchyme can also provide Notch ligands to the Lgr5 + CBCs in vivo. In case that is true, our proposed mechanism that Rfng promotes cell surface expression of Dll1 might be applicable to the mesenchymal cells too.
evidence: The claim is speculative, extending the proposed mechanism to mesenchymal cells based on inference.

claim: Upon loss of Rfng, reduced Dll1 expression on the cell surface of Paneth cells and mesenchymal cells would result in reduced Notch activity in the CBCs.
source: Upon loss Rfng, reduced Dll1 expression on the cell surface of Paneth cells and mesenchymal cells would result in reduced Notch activity in the CBCs, as observed.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the proposed mechanism and observed phenotype.

claim: The crypt cells are separated from the mesenchyme by the basement membrane.
source: However, the crypt cells are separated from the mesenchyme by the basement membrane.
evidence: The claim represents established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The efficacy of DLL mediated Notch signalling across the intestinal basement membrane needs to be explored.
source: The efficacy of DLL mediated Notch signalling across the intestinal basement membrane needs to be explored.
evidence: The claim identifies a knowledge gap that requires future investigation.

claim: LFNG in NICD- post-mitotic secretory cells of the upper crypt promotes Notch activity in the neighbouring enterocyte progenitors.
source: Although we have observed that the Lfng expressing cells are found both in the upper crypt and in the villus, our data suggests that LFNG in NICD- post-mitotic secretory cells of the upper crypt promotes Notch activity in the neighbouring enterocyte progenitors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the spatial expression data and functional studies.

claim: Notch signalling is not active in the villus.
source: As Notch signalling is not active in the villus, the Lfng+ cells of the villi likely do not impact epithelial cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about Notch signaling in the intestine.

claim: The Lfng+ cells of the villi likely do not impact epithelial cell differentiation.
source: As Notch signalling is not active in the villus, the Lfng+ cells of the villi likely do not impact epithelial cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of Notch activity in the villus.

claim: The reason secretory cells expressing Notch ligands and Lfng are found in the villi needs to be explored.
source: It would be interesting to explore the reason secretory cells expressing Notch ligands and Lfng are found in the villi.
evidence: The claim identifies a question for future investigation based on the observations.

claim: The differences, other than functional consequence, between the Lfng+ cells of the upper crypt and villus need to be explored.
source: The differences, other than functional consequence, between the Lfng+ cells of the upper crypt and villus needs to be explored.
evidence: The claim identifies a question for future investigation.

claim: Blocking the Notch pathway leads to serious GI related side effects.
source: Notch pathway is a potential therapeutic target, but blocking the pathway leads to serious GI related side effects (van Es et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to van Es et al., 2005, representing established knowledge.

claim: Targeting the Notch pathway through fringe appears to be a potentially viable strategy to exclusively modulate intestinal epithelial regeneration or its functions.
source: Targeting the Notch pathway through fringe appears to be a potentially viable strategy to exclusively modulate intestinal epithelial regeneration or its functions, absorption and mucus secretion, as Notch activity in the stem cells or progenitors can be specifically targeted by blocking Rfng or Lfng respectively.
evidence: The claim is speculative about therapeutic potential, based on inference from the findings.

claim: Notch activity in the stem cells or progenitors can be specifically targeted by blocking Rfng or Lfng respectively.
source: Targeting the Notch pathway through fringe appears to be a potentially viable strategy to exclusively modulate intestinal epithelial regeneration or its functions, absorption and mucus secretion, as Notch activity in the stem cells or progenitors can be specifically targeted by blocking Rfng or Lfng respectively.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the spatial expression patterns and functional effects of Rfng and Lfng.

claim: Fringe proteins provide another layer of spatial and lineage-specific modulation that might enhance robustness of intestinal homeostasis.
source: Even though Fringe proteins do not appear to be essential, they provide another layer of spatial and lineage-specific modulation that might enhance robustness of intestinal homeostasis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed spatial expression patterns and functional effects of Fringes.

claim: The highly robust regulation of Notch activity in the intestinal epithelium is consistent with inhibition of Notch1 or Dll1 only causing minor defective phenotype, while inhibition of Notch2, Dll4, Jag1, Hes1, Hes3 or Hes5 causes no significant phenotype.
source: This is consistent with the highly robust regulation of Notch activity in the intestinal epithelium as inhibition of Notch1 or Dll1 only causes minor defective phenotype, while inhibition of Notch2, Dll4, Jag1, Hes1, Hes3 or Hes5 causes no significant phenotype (Pellegrinet et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2010; Ueo et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pellegrinet et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2010; and Ueo et al., 2012, representing established knowledge.

claim: Secretory cells in the intestine, mainly enteroendocrine and goblet cells, are known to express Notch ligands, especially DLL1.
source: Secretory cells in the intestine, mainly enteroendocrine and goblet cells, are known to express Notch ligands, especially DLL1 (van Es et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to van Es et al., 2012, representing established knowledge.

claim: Suppression of Notch signalling is known to increase the goblet cell numbers.
source: Suppression of Notch signalling is known to increase the goblet cell numbers (van Es et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to van Es et al., 2005, representing established knowledge.

claim: Lfng silencing appears to lower Notch activity in the progenitors and promotes the secretory lineage leading to an increase in goblet cell numbers.
source: Therefore, Lfng silencing appears to lower Notch activity in the progenitors and promotes the secretory lineage leading to an increase in goblet cell numbers (Zheng et al., 2011; Kim and Shivdasani, 2011).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data and supported by citations to Zheng et al., 2011 and Kim and Shivdasani, 2011.

claim: Lfng may be secreted into the extracellular space.
source: Previous reports have indicated that Lfng may be secreted into the extracellular space (Shifley and Cole, 2008; Williams et al., 2016 ).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Shifley and Cole, 2008 and Williams et al., 2016, representing established knowledge.
